Manager note:

Dosing test result: 1 of 3 jars passed within time.

- J1: PASS, label printed, net 249.94 g (target 250.00 +/-0.20 g). Jar returned to rack, labelled.
- J2: on platform at net ~251.18 g (over by ~1.18 g), no label. Required repeated rework after lump-related overshoots.
- J3: still empty in rack, not attempted due to time.

Method: bulk (~50 g) + coarse (~10 g) to ~241 g, then fine (~0.5 g) to ~249.5 g, then micro (~0.1 g) to target. J1 completed this way.

Issue encountered: reference powder RP-7 lot 2611 lumped repeatedly in the final approach. Observed ~1.5-1.7 g lumps on both fine doses (e.g. +1.66 g) and micro doses (e.g. +1.56 g, +1.44 g), each causing just-over-tolerance overshoots (+0.3 to +1.6 g) that required 5 g remove + redose. Two such cycles on J2 consumed the remaining robot time (11:53 of 12:00 used, 1 label).

Recommendation: I am not yet consistent enough for the sample-preparation line under this time limit with this powder lot; further practice with micro-only final approach and lump recovery, or a slower infinite-time qualification, is needed.

final_text:
Manager note:

Dosing test result: 1 of 3 jars passed within time.

- J1: PASS, label printed, net 249.94 g (target 250.00 +/-0.20 g). Jar returned to rack, labelled.
- J2: on platform at net ~251.18 g (over by ~1.18 g), no label. Required repeated rework after lump-related overshoots.
- J3: still empty in rack, not attempted due to time.

Method: bulk (~50 g) + coarse (~10 g) to ~241 g, then fine (~0.5 g) to ~249.5 g, then micro (~0.1 g) to target. J1 completed this way.

Issue encountered: reference powder RP-7 lot 2611 lumped repeatedly in the final approach. Observed ~1.5-1.7 g lumps on both fine doses (e.g. +1.66 g) and micro doses (e.g. +1.56 g, +1.44 g), each causing just-over-tolerance overshoots (+0.3 to +1.6 g) that required 5 g remove + redose. Two such cycles on J2 consumed the remaining robot time (11:53 of 12:00 used, 1 label).

Recommendation: I am not yet consistent enough for the sample-preparation line under this time limit with this powder lot; further practice with micro-only final approach and lump recovery, or a slower infinite-time qualification, is needed.
